title: Segregated VPC endpoint policies and split-horizon DNS for control-plane
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Private control-plane installs must operate in environments that restrict cross-VPC service access. We previously relied on permissive VPC endpoint policies and a single Route53 forwarder, which caused over-broad service access (S3/STS) in highly regulated customers. This change introduces per-service, per-environment VPC endpoint policy templates plus a split-horizon DNS option that routes control-plane requests to an isolated interface endpoint in customer VPCs and normal tenant traffic to service endpoints. What this PR does: 1) Terraform: refactors terraform/modules/vpc_endpoints to support endpoint_policy_templates keyed by service and environment (dev/staging/prod). Adds least-privilege templates for s3, sts, kms, ssm, and secretsmanager. 2) DNS: adds an optional route53 split-horizon configuration (installer/templates/dns/split_horizon.tf) and documentation for deploying a private hosted zone with conditional forwarding for controlplane.redwood.internal. 3) Security groups: introduces a default least-privilege sg module used for interface endpoints and control-plane instances, with explicit ingress rules instead of open CIDR usage. 4) Helm: adds values.yaml knobs to enable endpoint-policy enforcement and pass a delegated zone name into the installer. 5) Migration and rollback: provides a non-destructive migration workflow (terraform plan to add policy attachments and then to enable split-horizon in a second apply) and a rollback plan that reverts feature flags and removes policy attachments. Testing: added integration tests that validate endpoint policy attachment and DNS resolution in a multi-account test harness. Backwards compatibility: feature flags default to off so existing installs are unaffected. Rollout plan: ship as a stage-gated opt-in in the private-installer chart, enable for pilot customers, collect logs, and then flip default to on in a future release. See docs/upgrade/vpc-endpoint-migration.md for the step-by-step migration guide and operator checklist. Risks and mitigations: initial terraform apply may trigger resource replacements for extremely old installs — migration doc includes detection and a safe plan to avoid replacement. CI notes: pipeline initially flagged a flaky multi-account test which was hardened (see commits).

release_notes: Added per-service VPC endpoint policy templates (s3, sts, kms, ssm, secretsmanager) — opt-in via helm values
Introduced split-horizon DNS support for control-plane hostnames to isolate control-plane traffic in customer VPCs
Least-privilege security group module for interface endpoints
migration_steps: 1) Review policies: run scripts/principal-discovery to enumerate existing principals
2) Apply terraform in plan mode to see attachments that will be created (do not apply yet)
3) Apply policy attachment step (no enablement of split-horizon): terraform apply -target=module.vpc_endpoints.policy_attachments
4) Validate access via integration tests in staging
5) Enable split-horizon feature flag in helm values and perform a controlled rollout to pilot tenants
6) Monitor DNS resolution and endpoint logs for 48 hours, then gradually expand
